# Recomposition twins

B6 synthetic templates and their resolvable B2 counterparts. Products are ORBIT / COMET and lumen-api; addresses are only documentation values in 192.0.2.0/24 and 2001:db8::/32. These fixtures establish no real-device result.

| Files | Mirrors | Entry / validation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `templates/*.json` | Original B6 synthetic examples; machine paths removed from the old index | Preserved examples, not admissible receipts or resolvable runtime artifacts |
| `author-*.km.json` | The two-layout KityMinder author source | Reuses text and structure from existing mind-map fixtures, with explicit synthetic automation identity; installed mindmap-format parser |
| `governing-spec.json`, `conflicting-spec.json`, `declarations.json`, `product-policy.json` | Product-authored governing sources and typed declaration positions | Exact product package bytes and publication proof, then current-line scope; no implicit priority |
| `adjudication.json` | A scripted independent decision template | Never self-attests acceptance; the test runs the actual adjudication workflow and binds genuine Hub records |
| `recompose-*.json` | Original, adapted, concretization and rebinding ledgers | `index.ts`, deterministic `write.ts`; runtime receipt identities supplied by the synthetic harness |
| `bed-b.json` | Second bed, structurally equal to the repository's first synthetic bed | Both manifests parse; recomposition bytes and decisions stay bed independent |
| `manifest.json` | File/digest index | Rebuilt with `write.ts`; contains relative paths only |

| Record | Expected terminal after genuine runtime evidence is bound |
| --- | --- |
| `recompose-pass.json` | Accepted, complete |
| `recompose-underdetermined.json` | Unknown; product author supplies verification knowledge before resubmission |
| `recompose-conflict.json` | Refused completion; declared adjudicator resolves applicability before resubmission |
| `recompose-missing-prerequisite.json` | Unknown/partial; compiler supplies prerequisites, not a case conflict |

The B6 examples contained placeholder selectors, paraphrased original ledgers and a self-described decision. `write.ts` preserves the original synthetic meanings, emits actual source hashes/selectors, retains verbatim original atoms and supplies declaration positions. Static settled decision references remain null until the end-to-end harness obtains genuine Hub receipts. No static JSON file is an admission credential. Old self-audit patterns and local paths in the original prose are not copied.

Regenerate: `node tests/fixtures/recompose/write.ts`. Audit every file: `node tests/fixtures/recompose/checks.ts`. The audit is a privacy scan only; production semantic classification uses declared structures and quoted model judgments. The old script was ported to TypeScript and public installed-skill interfaces rather than reintroducing a core default parser.
